newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish parties to outline anti-Islamist coalition.
newsitem.headline: Turkish parties to outline anti-Islamist coalition.

text.p: Members of three Turkish secularist parties were to begin drawing up the government programme of a planned anti-Islamist coalition on Friday and working out the distribution of ministries, party officials said.
"The commission will begin working today," an official from prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz's Motherland Party said.

Party sources say the government, a left-right coalition backed in parliament by another leftist party, will be ready to present a list of ministers to President Suleyman Demirel by next Monday or Tuesday.
But the alliance, to be led by Yilmaz, is still short of the simple majority it needs to win a vote of confidence over its pro-Islamist opponents.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned a week ago under pressure from the military. He plans to return to power in a coalition led by conservative Tansu Ciller.
